'''Dionisio Gallarati''' (May 8, 1923 – May 13, 2019) was an Italian [[mathematician]], who specialized in [[algebraic geometry]]. He was a major influence on the development of algebra and geometry at the [[University of Genova]].<ref name="Tucker Anderson">{{Cite book|author1=Martha A. Tucker|author2=Nancy D. Anderson|title=Guide to Information Sources in Mathematics and Statistics|date=30 September 2004|publisher=ABC-CLIO|isbn=978-0-313-05337-5|page=238}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Dionisio Gallarati |url=https://necrologie.ilsecoloxix.it/necrologi/2019/provincia-39-genova/citta-3132-genova/797474-gallarati-dionisio |publisher=Il Secoloxix |accessdate=20 July 2019}}</ref>

==Life==
Born May 8th 1923 in [[Savona]], [[Italy]], Gallarati joined the [[University of Pisa]] in 1941.  His studies being interrupted by the war, he received his first degree from Genova.<ref name="Mac">{{cite web |title=Dionisio Gallarati - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Gallarati/ |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]] |publisher=School of Mathematics and Statistics, [[University of St Andrews]] |access-date=27 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616010827/https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Gallarati/ |archive-date=16 June 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

He started his research career at [[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi|l'Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica]] in Rome, where he was taught by [[Giacomo Albanese]], [[Leonard Roth]], [[Leonida Tonelli]], [[E. G. Togliatti]], [[Beniamino Segre]] and [[Francesco Severi]].<ref name="Mac" />

He took a post at Genova in 1947, where he stayed until he retired in 1987.<ref name="Mac" />

==Research==
{{Expand section|date=August 2018}}
Gallarati published 64 papers between 1951 and 1996.

Important amongst his research was the study of surfaces in '''P'''<sup>3</sup> with multiple isolated singularities.  His lower bounds for maximal number of nodes of surfaces of degree ''n'' stood for a long time, and exact solutions for large ''n'' were still unknown in 2001.<ref name="Mac" />

In [[Grassmannian|Grassmannian geometry]] he extended Segre's bound "for the number of [[linearly independent]] complexes containing the curve in the [[Grassmannian]] corresponding to the tangent lines of a nondegenerate [[projective curve]]."<ref name="Mac" />  He extended the results to arbitrarily dimensioned [[Algebraic variety|varieties]]' tangent spaces, to higher degree complexes, and to arbitrary curves in Grassmannians corresponding to degenerate [[Scroll (mathematics)|scrolls]].<ref name="Mac" />

==Works==
{{Expand section|date=August 2018}}
Gallarati wrote three books<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?s=0&q=Gallarati%2C+Dionisio|title = zbMATH Open - the first resource for mathematics}}</ref> and 64 papers,<ref name="Mac" /> in algebraic geometry, [[differential geometry]], [[functional analysis]], [[group theory]], and biography.<ref name="MSN" />  His co-authors include Giulio Aruffo,  Mauro C. Beltrametti,  Maria Teresa Bonardi, Gabriella Canonero, Ettore Carletti, Enrica Casazza, Mario G. Galli, Aldo Monti Iandelli, Giacomo Bragadin, Giorgio Luigi Olcese, Giulio Passatore, Luigi Robert, Aldo Rollero, Michele Sarà, Giulio Scarsi and Maria Ezia Serpico.<ref name="MSN">{{Cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/MRAuthorID/70765|title=MR: Gallarati, Dionisio - 70765}}</ref>

33 of his papers are collected in ''Dionisio Gallarati: Collected Papers of Dionisio Gallarati'' Kinston, Ontario, 2000, ed A. V. Geramita.
